summary: 周六的话题集中在节点运行成本。Vitalik 提醒，现在半天就能同步一个以太坊节点，激进设置下磁盘占用可低于 0.5 TB；他还称 PeerDAS 近一年几乎零问题运行，是客户端开发者被低估的成就。nero_eth 介绍 Glamsterdam 的 snap v2：用区块级访问列表（本质上是状态差异）取代传统的修复阶段，同步更快更简单。

items.title: nero_eth：Glamsterdam 把 snap 同步提升一级
items.note: 08:15，snap v2 用区块级访问列表这种状态差异取代传统修复阶段；nero_eth：EIP-7928 已近最后一程 18:18，并行带来明显吞吐提升，同时兼容 zkEVM、部分有状态节点和包含列表。
items.title_en: nero_eth: Glamsterdam takes snap sync to the next level
items.note_en: 08:15, with snap v2 using the block-level access list, a state diff, to replace the traditional healing phase; nero_eth: EIP-7928 is approaching the final mile, 18:18, with significant throughput gains from parallelism and compatibility with zkEVMs, partially stateful nodes and inclusion lists.

keywords_en: PeerDAS running smoothly for nearly a year
summary_en: Saturday's discussion centered on the cost of running nodes. Vitalik noted you can now sync an Ethereum node in half a day, and with aggressive settings it takes under half a terabyte of disk; he also called PeerDAS running for nearly a year with basically no problems an underappreciated triumph of client developers. nero_eth described Glamsterdam's snap v2, which uses block-level access lists, essentially state diffs, to replace the traditional healing phase, making sync faster and simpler.
